tradition.name: Trap antillais
tradition.lineage: Martinican trap and Caribbean vocal crossover represented by Kalash, with Fort-de-France as selected practice center.

extras.description: Kalash’s trap and Caribbean crossover grounds this Antillean branch. The artist biography identifies a rapper and singer; his booking profile connects his upbringing to Fort-de-France. The authored production uses an 808-style low end and short synth figures beneath rap and response turns. This is one trap-oriented realization within a repertoire also spanning dancehall, not a claim that Antillean music has one uniform rhythm.

entries.geo_rationale: Selected documented practice center, not an exclusive origin or boundary of the discovery category.

tradition.name: Trap baiano
tradition.lineage: Feira de Santana-rooted rap/trap and R&B crossover represented by Duquesa’s independent-to-label recordings.

extras.description: Duquesa’s artist and booking accounts connect her to Feira de Santana and to rap, trap and R&B. In her direct interview about One Time she explains combining two proposed collaborations, with Onnika and Bivolt, over a beat produced by Go Dassisti. This authored trap-oriented model layers response turns over an 808-style drum and digital synth bed. It selects one branch of Bahia’s scene and does not infer pagode instruments from birthplace.
